Subject: Sudden p99 latency spikes, causing timeouts in production

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency and a higher error rate against the hosted inference endpoint for model 'redwood-13b-v1' around 15:45 PST. Several user flows time out (client-side timeouts), and our retry metrics also jumped — we're seeing cascading retries. This started impacting a small percentage of requests but it's critical for our SLAs.

Attached is a short extract from our APM plus a few sampled logs. Can you confirm whether there were any infra/rollouts that could explain this?

Summary:
- window: ~15:40-16:00 PST
- p95 up by ~400ms, p99 up by ~1.6s
- error rate (5xx) up from 0.1% to ~1.4% for that window

We appreciate any urgent help.

Thanks,
Jared
Customer Ops — Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 latency spikes, causing timeouts in production

Following up with an initial triage:
- No scheduled rollouts or kernel swaps between 15:00-17:00 PST in the hosted fleet.
- Host-level metrics (GPU load, network egress) do not show cluster-wide saturation. A small number of worker nodes showed higher queue depth around 15:45, but not enough to explain p99 delta across the entire region.
- I pulled request traces for Acme's API key and noticed a pattern: multiple short-lived connection attempts from the same client IPs with aggressive retry intervals. The request arrival pattern looks bursty rather than uniform.

I've attached a cropped log (acme-sdk-logs-20261102.txt) with examples showing repeated connect+retry within 200-400ms windows. That could amplify tail latency if upstream requests contend for runtime slots.

Next steps I'm doing now:
- Correlate our routing logs to see whether retries were hitting the same backends (hotspotting).
- Reconstruct tokenized request sizes to rule out payload-related slowdowns.

Would appreciate if Acme can share SDK version + timeout/retry config — that will speed up root-cause analysis.

-Dylan
Platform Reliability Engineer
Attachment: timeline-graph-20261103.png

Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 latency — immediate escalation

Jared — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We have engineering actively investigating. Two quick items while we dig in:

1) Can you confirm which Redwood SDK version you're using and whether you have any custom retry/backoff configured? Some older SDK versions defaulted to tight connect timeouts which, when combined with client-side retries, can create retry storms during transient slowdowns.

2) We're opening an internal incident (INF-4312) to track this and will update you within 4 hours with mitigation steps. If the impact is still affecting you, we can provide a temporary credit for the impacted window — I'll coordinate with your CS rep.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Sales Engineering

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Root cause analysis: client-side retries + aggressive timeouts amplified tail latency

Update from the infra investigation (summary):
- Root cause: Acme's integration was using the Redwood JS SDK v0.9.2 with default timeout/connect settings of 500ms and a retry policy that retries up to 3 times with minimal exponential backoff. During a transient backend scheduling hiccup at ~15:42 PST, many requests hit the same subset of backends because the client's retry logic retried immediately to the same endpoint. That produced a retry storm concentrated on a few worker nodes, increasing queue depth and pushing p99 higher.
- Our fleet did not have an underlying hardware failure; the pattern is consistent with client-side retry amplification.

Mitigation applied:
- Short-term (rolled within 90 minutes): throttled per-api-key concurrency for Acme to reduce hotspotting and applied a soft-rate limit at the edge to smooth arrival.
- Medium-term: added routing resilience changes to prefer cold-start-shifted backends if single-node queue depth exceeds threshold. PR: INF-4312.
- Customer guidance: ask Acme to upgrade SDK to v1.1.0 which increases default timeouts to 2s and implements jittered backoff; if immediate upgrade is not possible, set retry count to 1 and increase timeout to >=1500ms.

Evidence files attached: p99-digest-20261102.csv, acme-sdk-logs-20261102.txt.

Action items:
- Stephanie/Marcus: confirm communications to Acme and whether a credit is expected.
- Neha: prepare a short RCA with screenshots for the support portal.
- Dylan: follow up with a post-mortem and recommended SDK config in the public docs.

-Dylan

From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 17:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 latency — immediate escalation

Thanks team — we upgraded to SDK v1.1.0 and adjusted our retry policy per your recommendation (retries=1, timeout=2s with jitter). Our APM shows p99 back down to baseline within ~30 minutes of the change and error rate returned to normal.

We'll keep monitoring and report back if anything else crops up. Appreciate the quick triage and the guidance.

Best,
Jared
Acme Corp — Customer Ops
